title: Rotate an Array
prompt: A carousel needs to move the last k items to the front without changing the original list. Write a function that returns a new array rotated to the right by k steps.

explanation.beginner:
Example: rotateArray([1,2,3,4,5], 2) produces [4,5,1,2,3]. Reduce the rotation count modulo the length, then join the two slices in their new order. Handle empty input before taking a remainder.

Compare “wraps large k”: input [[1,2,3],4] produces [3,1,2]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Reduce the rotation count modulo the length, then join the two slices in their new order. Handle empty input before taking a remainder.

Tempting mistake: A count larger than the length still rotates by only its remainder. Empty input must not use modulo zero.

The reference uses slice. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost. Slicing and concatenation copy O(n) elements.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “wraps large k”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
